heading: Pennsylvania Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Pennsylvania paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Pennsylvania income tax, local earned income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable employee unemployment contributions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and provide your local tax information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Pennsylvania's local income tax system makes location particularly important when calculating net earnings. Employees receiving identical salaries may have different take-home pay because they live or work in different municipalities.

Whether you work in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Allentown or another Pennsylvania community, this calculator can help you compare salaries and manage your finances.

## How to Use the Pennsylvania Paycheck Calculator

Begin by entering your annual salary or hourly earnings before taxes.

Select your payment frequency. Enter the federal and Pennsylvania income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Enter the local earned income tax or Philadelphia Wage Tax amount shown on your pay stub. If both apply, enter the total withheld.

Include retirement contributions and healthcare premiums. Under Benefits, open Advanced settings and enter any Local Services Tax and employee unemployment contribution under Other deductions. Enter each deduction once.

Review your estimated gross pay, individual deductions and remaining take-home earnings.

Use your latest payroll statement and official local tax information for a more accurate estimate.

## Pennsylvania Payroll Taxes in 2026

Higher-income employees may also encounter Additional Medicare withholding.

The exact deductions depend on your taxable earnings, residency, work location and employee benefit arrangements.

## How Pennsylvania State Income Tax Works

Pennsylvania applies a flat individual income tax rate of 3.07%.

Unlike states that use progressive tax brackets, Pennsylvania generally applies the same statutory rate to all applicable taxable compensation.

For example, an employee receiving $2,500 in Pennsylvania taxable wages would have ordinary state withholding of:

$2,500 × 3.07% = $76.75.

Pennsylvania does not automatically follow every federal deduction rule. Certain employee retirement contributions that reduce federal income-taxable wages may remain taxable compensation for Pennsylvania purposes.

A reliable Pennsylvania salary calculator must therefore maintain separate federal and state taxable wage amounts.

Read the official [Pennsylvania employer withholding guidance](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/resources/tax-types-and-information/employer-withholding) and [personal income tax guide](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/resources/tax-types-and-information/personal-income-tax) for additional information.

## Pennsylvania Local Earned Income Tax

Pennsylvania's Act 32 framework requires employers to account for applicable municipal and school district earned income taxes.

For ordinary employment covered by Act 32, employers compare the employee's total resident earned income tax rate with the nonresident earned income tax rate applicable to the workplace.

The higher of these two rates generally determines withholding.

Suppose your resident earned income tax rate is 1% and your workplace's nonresident rate is 1.5%.

The applicable withholding rate would generally be 1.5%, not the combined 2.5%.

For $2,500 of covered earnings, the resulting local withholding would be $37.50.

These rates are hypothetical. Use the official [Pennsylvania local tax information and address lookup resources](https://dced.pa.gov/local-government/local-income-tax-information/) to identify your actual tax jurisdiction.

The [Pennsylvania local withholding FAQs](https://dced.pa.gov/local-government/local-income-tax-information/local-withholding-tax-faqs/) explain the residence and workplace rate comparison.

## Understanding Pennsylvania PSD Codes

Political Subdivision codes, commonly known as PSD codes, identify Pennsylvania municipalities for local income tax administration.

Your employer uses residence and employment location information to determine applicable withholding rates and direct payments to the correct tax collector.

A ZIP code alone may not establish your correct local tax jurisdiction.

When entering local tax information, use your official residence and workplace tax classifications rather than relying on a nearby city's published rate.

The [Pennsylvania residency certification form](https://dced.pa.gov/download/residency-certification-form-local-earned-income-tax-withholding-pdf/?wpdmdl=57773) explains the information used by employers.

## Philadelphia Paycheck Calculator

Philadelphia operates its own Wage Tax system rather than simply following the ordinary Act 32 withholding calculation.

The applicable 2026 rates are:

Residents are generally subject to the tax on applicable earned income, while nonresidents may owe the tax on qualifying work performed in Philadelphia.

For $2,500 of covered earnings after July 1, 2026:

Philadelphia resident withholding is approximately $93.38.

Philadelphia nonresident withholding is approximately $85.63.

The correct calculation depends on the payment date and employee circumstances.

Review the official [Philadelphia Wage Tax rates and employer guidance](https://www.phila.gov/services/business-self-employment/business-taxes/wage-tax-employers/) before entering local tax information.

## Pennsylvania Local Services Tax

Some Pennsylvania municipalities collect a Local Services Tax, commonly abbreviated LST.

Unlike ordinary earned income tax, this is generally a fixed annual amount rather than a percentage of wages.

For illustration, an annual Local Services Tax of $52 distributed across 26 biweekly paychecks would produce a $2 deduction per paycheck.

Certain income exemptions, multiple-employer rules and collection requirements can affect the amount withheld.

Do not assume that every Pennsylvania employee pays $52 annually.

Consult the [Pennsylvania local tax requirements for employers](https://dced.pa.gov/local-government/local-income-tax-information/instructions-employers/) for official guidance.

## Pennsylvania Employee Unemployment Contributions

Pennsylvania requires covered employees to contribute toward its unemployment compensation system.

For 2026, the employee contribution rate is 0.07% of gross covered wages.

Unlike some other state unemployment contribution systems, Pennsylvania does not impose an annual wage ceiling on this employee deduction.

Employer unemployment contributions are separate from the employee contribution.

Visit the official [Pennsylvania unemployment compensation yearly tax highlights](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dli/resources/for-employers-and-educators/how-to-file/uc-tax/yearly-tax-highlights) for the applicable annual rate.

## Federal Payroll Taxes for Pennsylvania Employees

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable wages, payment frequency, filing status and Form W-4 information.

The ordinary employee Social Security contribution is 6.2% of covered wages up to $184,500 in 2026.

Medicare generally applies at 1.45% of covered wages without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers also generally withhold an additional 0.9% once Medicare wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t), the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and the [Social Security Administration wage base information](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html).

## Pennsylvania Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually with 26 biweekly payments.

Assume ordinary single federal withholding settings, no additional benefit deductions, an applicable local earned income tax rate of 1%, and a $52 annual Local Services Tax.

The local tax assumptions are illustrative and do not represent every Pennsylvania municipality.

Use your actual tax jurisdiction and benefit information when estimating your paycheck.

## Pennsylvania Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose an employee earns $25 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus eight qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $1,000.

Overtime earnings: $300.

Total gross earnings: $1,300.

Assuming all earnings are subject to Pennsylvania income tax, ordinary state withholding would be $39.91.

The employee unemployment contribution would be $0.91.

Federal taxes and applicable local deductions would also reduce the paycheck.

Review the [US Department of Labor overtime requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about eligibility and exemptions.

## Working Across Pennsylvania State Borders

Pennsylvania has reciprocal income tax agreements with Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, Ohio, Virginia and West Virginia.

These arrangements may affect the state income tax treatment of qualifying employee compensation.

However, state reciprocity does not automatically remove Pennsylvania local earned income taxes.

Eligible employees should follow the applicable withholding exemption and documentation requirements.

Consult the [Pennsylvania income withholding guide](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/forms-and-publications/pa-personal-income-tax-guide/income-subject-withholding-estimated-payments-penalties-interest-other-additions) before applying an interstate exemption.

## Managing Your Pennsylvania Take-Home Income

Compare employment offers using estimated net income rather than gross salary alone.

Account for differences in municipal taxes, housing expenses, commuting costs and employee benefits.

Use our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) to establish a savings target and our [debt-to-income ratio calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate your borrowing commitments.

The [CFPB consumer financial education resources](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/) can also help you prepare a practical [household budget](/calculators/budget-calculator/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Pennsylvania's state income tax rate in 2026?

Pennsylvania applies a flat individual income tax rate of 3.07% to applicable taxable compensation.

### Do all Pennsylvania employees pay the same local income tax?

No. Applicable local taxes depend on residence, employment location and municipal rules. Philadelphia also operates a separate Wage Tax system.

### How much is Pennsylvania employee unemployment withholding?

The 2026 employee contribution rate is 0.07% of gross covered wages, without an annual wage ceiling.
